analysis.title: PrimeView: Hedge Funds Add to AI Hedging Shorts
key_insights: On Friday hedge funds kept cutting AI beta, led by Semis (-0.8std), Memory (-1.0std) and Hardware (-1.2std). Flows shifted from more than 90% long selling to roughly 50/50 long selling and shorting.

Hyperscalers were small net bought (+0.3std) as hedge funds focused on higher-quality names with available compute and stronger build profiles. UBS says this extends the trend seen since early October.

Power names were net bought (+1.7std), with about 70% of flows from long buying. UBS describes hedge funds as bottom-fishing selectively and adding relative-value (RV) trades across the AI value chain.

Hedge funds added +1.9std of gross exposure to US equities, the 6th-largest re-risking day YTD. The add came from +2std of short exposure and +1std of long exposure, so it was largely a market-neutral/RV risk add rather than a directional bet.
Friday saw the largest increase in hedge fund short exposure since June 15, before the summer unwind.

UBS Head of Cash Equity Trading Zain Nizami remains cautious as correlations rise. The risk is that crowded sector and RV trades, particularly Semis vs. Software and Semis vs. Hyperscalers, spill over into broader portfolio de-risking.
Nizami recommends buying Semis while selling the recent 'hedging beneficiaries'. Net exposure in Semis is back near July and Liberation Day lows, while Hyperscaler and Software exposures remain high.

sector_views.rationale: UBS cash equity trading recommends buying Semis. Net exposure is back near July and Liberation Day lows, which UBS calls attractive from a positioning perspective.
Nizami recommends selling the recent 'hedging beneficiaries'. Hyperscaler exposure remains high, and the Semis vs. Hyperscalers RV trade is flagged as crowded.
Software exposure remains high, and the Semis vs. Software RV trade is flagged as crowded, with spillover risk to broader de-risking.
